messages:
sam_support: Heads-up — acme-corp PROD reports 403s on SSO callback since their IdP did a cert rollover ~15m ago. They say users get redirected back to our /saml/acs and see 403. Can we triage?
lee_infra: Can you paste the SAML error from our auth logs and their IdP metadata XML?
sam_support: Paste of the auth-service log snippet:```
[2026-03-17T17:02:11Z] auth.saml: ERROR InvalidSignature: signature verification failed for assertion; expected thumbprint=AB:12:CD:34:EF got=FF:EE:DD:CC:BB  
request_id=req_43921 user=acme-corp relaystate=...
```
sam_support: Their IdP metadata (redacted) snippet:```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme-corp.example">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo><X509Data><X509Certificate>MIIC...OLD_CERT...</X509Certificate></X509Data></KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <SingleSignOnService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect" Location="https://idp.acme-corp.example/sso"/>
    <AssertionConsumerService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST" Location="http://auth.redwood.ai/saml/acs" index="0"/>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
anya_prod: Notable: their ACS in metadata is http:// (not https). We normally expect https://auth.redwood.ai/saml/acs and we canonicalize ACSs on ingest. If they rotated cert and also changed metadata to include the literal http: ACS that could explain mismatch if our config uses strict ACS matching.
chris_security: From the logs it looks like signature didn't match new cert. But also the ACS mismatch could trigger our auth code path that rejects assertions early. Two separate issues: (1) cert thumbprint mismatch -> need metadata refresh; (2) ACS value mismatch -> we may be strictly validating recipient against stored ACS list.
sam_support: Repro steps I used against staging:```
# fetch metadata
curl -sS https://idp.acme-corp.example/metadata.xml -o am.xml
# post a SAMLResponse captured from browser (sanitized)
curl -v -X POST -F "SAMLResponse=@response.b64" -F "RelayState=..." https://auth.redwood.ai/saml/acs
```
lee_infra: Can we force a metadata refresh for that tenant and clear the idp cache? In past cases our metadata-fetcher ignored a 200+gzip header change and didn't update because of stale ETag logic. Will force refetch and restart auth-service instance for that tenant.
deploy-bot: auth-service v2.14.0 deployed 10 minutes ago to prod (commit: 9f4b2d).
chris_security: Quick mitigation options: add their http:// ACS as an allowed alternate for their tenant or temporarily relax strict recipient-check for the tenant while we refresh metadata and verify certs. Prefer to avoid disabling signature checks.
lee_infra: Doing force refresh now — hitting their metadata endpoint with cache-bypass and saving new xml. Also clearing local idp cache for tenant id acme-corp.```
# commands run
curl -s -H 'Cache-Control: no-cache' https://idp.acme-corp.example/metadata.xml -o /tmp/acme-metadata.xml
kubectl exec -it deploy/auth-service -- curl -fsS localhost:8080/admin/refresh-idp?tenant=acme-corp
kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service
```
lee_infra: Restart done, waiting for pods to stabilize.
lee_infra: After restart — ran a test login for a user and saw 302 -> 200, no 403. Auth log snippet:```
[2026-03-17T17:04:12Z] auth.saml: INFO Assertion accepted for user=jdoe@acme-corp
[2026-03-17T17:04:12Z] auth.saml: INFO Issuer matched https://idp.acme-corp.example cert_thumbprint=FF:EE:DD:CC:BB
```
sam_support: Customer confirmed they're able to login again. They said they updated metadata to point to http vs https during their change; we accepted updated cert and refreshed ACS mapping but we should follow up on ACS protocol mismatch.
anya_prod: Action items: (1) schedule a small change to allow our metadata ingestion to normalize ACS Location protocol (http -> https) and warn instead of rejecting, (2) add detection to metadata refresher to ignore stale ETag/gzip changes, (3) postmortem with acme-corp to confirm why their ACS changed protocol during cert rotation.
chris_security: I'll open SEV2 tracking ticket (SEC-1421) for the postmortem and add recommended mitigation (no disabling signature checks).
sam_support: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll follow up with acme-corp support ticket and mark this thread resolved once the PM for metadata ingestion signs off.
